definition: Incisive means direct, sharp, and precise, especially in analysis or comment; cutting straight to the point.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word incisive. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know incisive should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: One incisive question from the back row exposed the flaw the whole committee had missed.
Clear is weaker than incisive: a clear comment is easy to follow, while an incisive one also cuts to the exact point that matters.
Piercing is stronger than incisive — a piercing insight seems to go straight through every defense to something hidden, while incisive analysis makes one clean, precise cut.

Penetrating describes the seeing: a penetrating mind or question reaches past surfaces into the heart of a matter. Incisive describes the delivery — analysis that cuts straight to the decisive point in a few exact words. Insight can be penetrating yet fog-bound; incisive comment is sharp on the page.

Sharp is the everyday, all-purpose word for a keen mind or pointed remark. Incisive is more specific praise: it says the analysis itself cuts — direct, precise, and aimed at the one point that decides the question, not merely quick or clever in passing.
